intro: I create these synthetic datasets because real hospital, finance, and business data is private and hard to access for practice. Each dataset is designed with realistic logic — not just random numbers — so learners can practice SQL, Python, and BI tools on data that actually behaves like the real world.

datasets.name: Gurugram Hospital Analytics Dataset
datasets.problem_statement: Real hospital data is private and rarely available for public learning due to patient confidentiality. I wanted to build a realistic, logically accurate hospital dataset so learners can practice healthcare analytics.

dataset_structure.desc: OPD/IPD patient records with disease & billing info

challenges: Injecting controlled raw data issues (3-6%) for cleaning practice
insights: Average patient waiting time by category (Appointment vs Walk-in)
Disease patterns by season (monsoon diseases in June)

datasets.name: Indian Financial Fraud Dataset
datasets.problem_statement: Real banking transaction data with fraud labels is extremely hard to access publicly due to strict data privacy and RBI compliance regulations. I built a 250,000-row realistic synthetic dataset mimicking real-world Indian banking patterns — card usage, geographical anomalies, and multi-entity relational schemas — so learners can practice fraud analytics without any data privacy concerns.

dataset_structure.desc: Customer demographics, occupation, segment, and state/city info
Credit limits, card status (Active/Blocked/Expired/Lost), card type & mode
Merchant category, risk level, ratings, and location
Primary transaction table linked via Customer_ID, Card_ID & Merchant_ID (~5% fraud target)

datasets.python_snippet:
# Detecting card status violations - common fraud signal
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('Transaction_Data_250k.csv')
cards = pd.read_csv('Cards_Data.csv')

merged = df.merge(cards, on='Card_ID', how='left')

# Flag transactions attempted on blocked/expired/lost cards
risky_status = ['Blocked', 'Expired', 'Lost']
merged['Status_Violation'] = merged['Card_Status'].isin(risky_status).astype(int)

fraud_rate = merged.groupby('Status_Violation')['Is_Fraud'].mean()
print(fraud_rate)
challenges: Designing a realistic 4-table relational schema (Customer, Card, Merchant, Transaction) with consistent foreign key logic
Injecting fraud signals that mimic real patterns — card status violations, credit limit breaches, geo/time anomalies, merchant risk spikes, and transaction velocity issues
Keeping fraud class imbalance realistic (~5%) to allow practice with SMOTE, ADASYN, and cost-sensitive learning techniques
Simulating late-night transactions with location mismatches without making the pattern too obvious for ML models
insights: Fraud patterns vary significantly across channels — POS, UPI, and Online Web transactions each show different risk signatures
High-risk merchant categories (Airlines, Hotels, Electronics) show sudden spending spikes correlated with fraud
Rapid successive transactions (velocity fraud) combined with authentication failures are strong fraud predictors
Dataset enables building Power BI/Tableau risk-monitoring dashboards alongside ML classification models
